status: DRAFT 2026-11-15: not declared, not run. Needs runner support (see implementation_required) and the open decisions before declaration.
supersedes: none yet. strict-v6 results and the strict-v7 draft (v6 cells with two rule fixes) are kept. v8 is a redesign after the v6 audit.
seed_rule: condition j (order of this file): seed0 + j; the same perturbation array for every engine, rung and repeat

engines.open_decision: whether MuJoCo Warp 3.17 is also run (v6 found ~0.3 % of 4.0 rollouts with a ~60-mm spurious contact, none in 3.17)

design_rule: every test is a provable statement of the rigid-body Coulomb model; points are placed by margin to an analytic boundary; anything the theory cannot decide is recorded but not scored

fixed.geometry: assets/round_socket_exact (32-gon bore, inscribed radius 12.000 mm, base z 0-10 mm, wall z 10-40 mm, outer radius 50 mm); peg = cylinder radius 12 mm - clearance, half-length 25 mm, solid-cylinder inertia
fixed.frame: all poses in the tilt plane through a flat-face centre of the bore (azimuth 5.625 deg); centre_inplane_mm along that direction; tilt_deg leans the peg top toward the negative in-plane direction
fixed.release: at rest, gravity only (gravity = 9.81 m/s^2 x gravity_scale), 3-s run. W: exact two-point contact. R: bottom face on the rim top. C: lowest point 2 mm above the rim top

rules.unit_of_analysis: the CONDITION, not the rollout. R = 8 rollouts per condition (perturbation U(+-0.05 mm) perpendicular to the tilt plane, identical arrays for all engines) exist only to detect instability. A condition is 'correct' iff every rollout of every repeat matches the label, 'wrong' iff none does, 'unstable' otherwise. No rollout-level totals or rollout-level confidence intervals are reported.

outcome_taxonomy.held: max drop <= 5 mm AND max tilt change <= 5 deg AND settled
outcome_taxonomy.seated_settled: final centre z <= 36 mm AND settled
outcome_taxonomy.seated_unsettled: final centre z <= 36 mm AND NOT settled (reported separately from never reaching the seat)
outcome_taxonomy.partial: inside or on the socket, neither held nor seated
outcome_taxonomy.tipped_or_ejected: rim cells that left the release pose without seating, or centre radial > 50 mm
outcome_taxonomy.invalid: non-finite state, contact-buffer truncation, or tunnelling through the socket

rules.settled: over the last 0.5 s: centre z range <= 0.5 mm, centre speed <= 5 mm/s AND tilt range <= 0.5 deg (v6 ignored rotation). Creep rate (mm/s) and tilt rate (deg/s) over that window are reported for every rollout.

correct_rule.inserted: seated_settled AND final radial <= clearance + 0.01 mm AND final tilt within 0.5 deg of a member of final_state_set.tilt_deg (flat only, or flat / leaning where the cell's mu makes a leaning rest admissible)
correct_rule.unlabelled (expected = null): never scored; outcome recorded to locate the flip

rules.fidelity_metrics_reported_for_every_cond: max displacement and max tilt change (analytic value 0 for every 'held' label), strict-hold count (<= 0.5 mm and <= 0.5 deg), final z / tilt / radial excess for seated pegs, time from release to first base contact for control cells (analytic 80.8 ms). These are reported next to the label result and are never hidden behind a tolerance.
rules.penetration: computed from the peg POSE by one shared routine against the analytic socket (base plane, 32-gon bore, rim top), every step, identically for all engines; split by region (base / bore wall / rim top), not by contact normal. Reported: peak, 99th percentile over time, time above 0.1 mm. Engine-reported contact depth is kept only as a secondary column; any engine contact deeper than pose-based penetration + 1 mm is flagged as a spurious contact and counted.

universal_checks_every_rollout.non_penetration: pose-based penetration (see 'penetration'): distance of the peg pose outside the set of non-penetrating poses, in mm and as a fraction of the clearance
universal_checks_every_rollout.energy: m g z + kinetic energy (from the logged per-step pose) must never exceed its initial value by more than 1 % of m g x 32 mm; violations are counted and the largest gain reported
universal_checks_every_rollout.admissible_rest: the final pose is classified against the rigid equilibrium classes: seated flat; seated leaning (allowed only if mu >= lean_rest_possible_above_mu); two-point wedge at the final tilt (allowed only if mu >= mu*(final tilt)); upright on the rim (allowed only if the final centre offset >= the rim threshold); lying on its side on the socket top; left the socket. A rest in a class the rigid model forbids at this mu is an 'inadmissible rest'; a pose matching no class is listed as 'unclassified'. This is the only correctness statement made for unlabelled conditions.

rules.criteria_freeze: every threshold above is fixed at declaration. Smoke tests may use the selection conditions only. If a label is contested after the run, the condition is dropped for all engines, never relabelled. Any other change makes a new revision.

regularisation_ladder.principle: candidates are defined by a measured observable, not by engine parameters, so both engines search the same range of regularisation. Each rung is one fixed configuration.

calibration_cell.note: 32-mm centred drop; not a scored condition

regularisation_ladder.tolerance: pose-based peak base penetration within 10 % of the target on the calibration cell
regularisation_ladder.damping_alignment: after first base contact the peg must stay within 0.05 mm of its final height from 0.3 s onward (no long ringing)
regularisation_ladder.sap_warp: bisect ke; tau = smallest of {1.5, 3, 6, 12, 24} ms that meets damping_alignment; gap = 0.1 mm
regularisation_ladder.mujoco_warp: bisect solref timeconst with dampratio = 1; solimp = 0.95 0.95 0.001 0.5 2; integrator = implicitfast, cone = elliptic, solver = Newton. timeconst < 2 * dt is not allowed (MuJoCo's own limit): such a rung is recorded as 'unreachable at this dt' and is not replaced.

run_plan.structure: task_runner_sop.md phases: B = 1 audit, B = 5 selection on a few selection-only conditions, then the frozen configuration on the disjoint frozen matrix. Candidates are never run on the frozen matrix.

1_selection.why_these: three labelled conditions at the dev clearance (0.3 mm), each close to an analytic boundary and together pulling in opposite directions: a wedge that must slide in and seat (0.8 mu*), a wedge that must stay (1.25 x unique-hold edge), a rim rest just outside the stability threshold (x1.10). A configuration that is too soft or too sticky fails at least one of them.
1_selection.selection_rule: most selection conditions 'correct'; then fewest 'unstable'; then fewest inadmissible rests; then lowest mean pose-based peak penetration over the selection conditions; then declared order. B = k is the same rule over the first k candidates (kept in the raw artifact); B = 1 is the native default, B = 5 the frozen configuration.
1_selection.smoke: code smoke tests may use these selection conditions only; no frozen condition is run before the configuration is frozen

2_frozen_matrix.conditions: every condition with role = 'frozen' (same clearance as selection: transfer to other poses / frictions / loads; clearances 0.1 and 1.0 mm: transfer to unseen geometry). Reported separately for the two groups.
configurations: native default (B = 1), unless it is the winner

3_robustness.dt: frozen B = 5 at dt = 0.25 and 1.0 ms on the robustness subset (a configuration that violates an engine limit at that dt is recorded as not runnable, not retuned)
3_robustness.repeat: frozen B = 5 run a second time on the robustness subset to expose run-to-run non-determinism

run_plan.4_attribution_control: MuJoCo only, selection conditions only: the 0.6-mm rung's solref with native integrator / cone / solver, to separate stiffness from solver options

reports.0_selection_table: per engine: all five candidates on the selection conditions (correct / wrong / unstable, pose-based penetration), the frozen index and what changed from B = 1.
reports.1_hardness_correctness_curve: selection conditions only (three conditions, descriptive): outcome versus measured pose-based penetration for the five candidates, both engines on the same axis. Next to it: stop time after first base contact on the calibration cell, against 2 ms and 10 ms marks.
reports.2_frozen_result: B = 1 and frozen B = 5 on the frozen matrix: labelled conditions correct / wrong / unstable per block, split into same-clearance and unseen-clearance groups; inadmissible rests on every condition including the unlabelled ones.
reports.3_boundary_location: W: per engine and clearance, which of the five friction points slide / hold and whether the flip lies inside admissible_flip_band [mu*, unique-hold lower edge]. Non-monotone sweeps are flagged. R: the offset interval containing the flip, and its distance from the analytic threshold in mm and in units of the clearance.
reports.4_invariance: I: largest gravity scale (1, 8, 64) and mass scale at which the outcome still equals the base cell's; whether the mirror image gives the same outcome.
reports.5_mechanism_diagnostics: R: innermost peg contact point two steps after release versus the analytic support edge (support-edge error, mm). All blocks: spurious-contact count; pose-based versus engine-reported penetration; for MuJoCo the residual against kappa * v * timeconst.
reports.6_robustness: dt = 0.25 / 0.5 / 1.0 ms and the repeat run on the robustness subset.

not_covered: Geometric interference (a peg larger than the bore being squeezed in): with a flat-ended peg and a sharp-edged bore the block is face-on-face, so it cannot probe bore-wall penetration. It needs a tapered or chamfered asset; block L (load scaling of self-locked holds) is the available substitute.
Slide-phase trajectory reference, restitution, impact force and duration (levels 2-4): out of scope by decision; restitution is covered by the bounce tasks.

Free fall only: no gripper compliance, no applied insertion force, no controller. Impact at 0.2-0.8 m/s is not how a robot inserts; static penetration under a 10-50 N push is not exercised except through gravity scaling in block I. A compliantly held, driven insertion is the planned next task.

Blindness: clearances 0.1 and 0.3 mm were never run (1.0 mm was, with other tilts and frictions), and the blocks were designed knowing v6's findings (SAP's rim support gap, MuJoCo's soft-contact behaviour). This is disclosed, not removable.

W resolution: the rigid model itself is non-unique over a factor 2-5 in mu between mu* and the unique-hold edge, so a flip anywhere inside that band is consistent with theory. Only R has a sharp analytic boundary.
No real data: every reference is the rigid-body Coulomb limit.
implementation_required: socket_v8_common.py: outcome taxonomy, condition-level scoring, flip location, shared pose-based penetration

both runners: per-step pose logging, gravity_scale, mass_kg and azimuth per condition, calibration stage for the ladder, selection -> freeze -> frozen-matrix driver, contact-point dump for block R, engine-contact-depth column
optional: batch conditions that share a model (R offsets, L scales where the engine allows) as worlds; must be shown on dev to leave results unchanged
